title: Wavefront kernel sampler and eviction-probing for resilient paged KV caches
creator: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: paged attention workloads show periodic tail-latency spikes caused by suboptimal kernel selection during decode waves and by noisy eviction behavior in the KV page pool. This ticket implements a wavefront-aware kernel sampling layer paired with lightweight eviction-probing to reduce decode jitter and increase effective KV reuse across interleaved requests. The approach is intentionally incremental and backward-compatible with existing kernel routing: a sampler recommends candidate kernels and an eviction-prober briefly probes residency impact before committing to page reclamation. Goals: reduce 95th/99th token latency by ~15-25% on mixed long-short workloads, reduce unnecessary page churn, and maintain stable throughput under bursty traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test: kernel sampler returns top-2 candidate kernels within 50us median decision time under 8-gpu host
SLO: 95th-token-latency improvement >= 12% on mixed seq-length benchmark vs baseline runtime-1.18 under 80% load
Eviction churn (page evict re-populate cycles per minute) reduced by >= 20% on multi-tenant sim workload
No regressions in end-to-end token correctness or model outputs (unit eval suite pass)
Can be toggled by runtime config flags without restart and has metrics exposed in Console
design_decisions: Sampler model: lightweight heuristics + recent-history scoring (no ML model in first phase). Use per-tenant short-term histograms for sequence length and prefix hit rate.

Wavefront concept: track active decode windows (wavefronts) per GPU to bias kernel choice toward low-latency kernels when the wavefront deadline is tight; prefer throughput kernels when wavefront has slack.

Eviction-probing: before evicting a candidate page, perform a cheap simulated access metric (probe) to estimate reuse probability; if probe indicates high reuse, defer eviction or migrate to a low-priority shard.
Backpressure interaction: sampler recommendations honor prefill/backpressure signals and explicit per-request latency budgets supplied by the API layer.
Observability: expose sampler decisions, probe outcomes, and per-page reuse score as metrics (histograms/gauges) and log samples for debugging.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 2 days): implement sampler prototype in the runtime with hooks for wavefront state and per-tenant histograms. Add microbench harness and synthetic load generator to emulate mixed workloads.
Phase 2 (core, 6 days): integrate eviction-prober which runs as optimistic check before page reclamation, implement quick migrate-to-cold-shard path, add flags to toggle sampler/prober independently.
Phase 3 (hardening, 4 days): add unit and integration tests, instrument metrics and traces, add graceful fallback to legacy kernel selection when sampler errors occur.
Phase 4 (canary, 3 days): deploy to a small dedicated pool (internal) with traffic mirroring, collect metrics and adjust heuristic thresholds, run correctness evals.
Phase 5 (rollout, 2 days): staged rollout across dedicated regions with runtime flags; monitor regressions and rollback thresholds configured.
testing_plan: Microbench: end-to-end decode latency with synthetic interleaved long/short sequences and multi-tenant contention
Replay tests: run production trace replay on staging pool with precise instrumentation to capture eviction churn and kernel-switch frequency
A/B canary: 10% traffic on Canary pool vs baseline for 48 hours with alerting on latency/regression
Stress: sustained 2x burst load to validate sampler does not add CPU contention or increase tail latencies beyond acceptable limits
Correctness: run model regression suite and sample token outputs across kernels to ensure deterministic behavior for supported models
rollout_plan: Start with opt-in runtime flag for internal-only dedicated clusters. After 48h of stable metrics and no correctness regressions, enable for low-traffic host pools, then gradual ramp to 100% for dedicated. For hosted customers, gate behind canary regions and feature toggle. Provide Runbook with rollback steps and threshold-based alerts.
notes: 2025-02-12 - Spike complete: prototype sampler reduced kernel switch rate by ~18% in isolated microbench. Observed small CPU overhead (~3%) on control plane thread.
2025-02-18 - Decision: proceed with heuristic-only sampler for Phase 1; ML-driven scoring deferred to future ticket if heuristics plateau.

2025-03-01 - Eviction-prober design updated to avoid synchronous probes during heavy GC windows; probes run opportunistically on low-priority worker.
2025-03-04 - Canary readiness: metrics dashboard stubbed, smoke tests passing on internal pool. Preparing runbook and canary alerts.
